front: Blood Brothers has three sub-plots that run alongside the main plot. What are they?
answer: Sammy's criminal life / Mrs Lyons' paranoia / Linda's relationships
title: Plot, Structure & Genre

front: Blood Brothers uses six dramatic conventions to create meaning. Name them.
answer: Dramatic irony / Marking the moment / Passage of time / Cross-cutting / Duologue / Monologue
title: Plot, Structure & Genre

front: Why does Blood Brothers use a cyclical structure that starts with the twins' deaths?
answer: It shows the tragic outcome is inevitable, reinforcing the play's central theme of fate.
title: Plot, Structure & Genre

front: Why did 1980s musicals need big casts and dramatic moments?
answer: Funding cuts to theatre meant producers needed spectacle to attract large audiences.
title: Plot, Structure & Genre

front: Which five key scenes should you focus on to revise character development in Blood Brothers?
items: Mrs Johnstone gives her baby away
Mrs Johnstone gives Edward the locket
answer: Mrs Johnstone gives her baby away / Mickey and Edward become friends / Mrs Johnstone gives Edward the locket / Mickey in prison / The final scene
title: Characters

front: What three key moments define Linda's character arc in Blood Brothers?
items: Standing up for Mickey as a child
Watching him fall apart after prison
answer: Standing up for Mickey as a child / Marrying Mickey / Watching him fall apart after prison
title: Characters

front: Why does Russell give Mickey and Edward such similar childhoods but different adult lives?
answer: To argue that nurture, not nature, determines what happens to a person, despite identical genes.
title: Characters

front: Why does Mrs Lyons become increasingly paranoid and unstable across the play?
answer: Guilt and fear of losing Edward destroy her from within, driving her toward violence.
title: Characters

front: Blood Brothers shows cultural context through three details. What are they?
answer: Going to the cinema / Playing on the streets / Marilyn Monroe songs
title: Themes & Context

front: Which three locations does Russell use to show the class divide in Blood Brothers?
answer: Liverpool city centre (Johnstones) / Wealthier Liverpool (Lyons) / Skelmersdale (later rehousing)
title: Themes & Context

front: Why does Russell include the police officer scene in Blood Brothers?
answer: To show the system judges the same behaviour differently depending on a family's social class.
title: Themes & Context

front: Why does Russell leave it ambiguous whether fate or the class system caused the twins' deaths?
answer: So the audience must decide for themselves what really caused the tragedy.
title: Themes & Context

front: Blood Brothers uses six colours with symbolic meaning in costume design. Name them.
answer: Red / Blue / Pink / Black / Yellow / White
title: Costume, Hair & Make-up

front: Why do Mickey and Edward wear similar clothing types as children but with different quality?
answer: So the audience can see the class divide at a glance, without a word being spoken.
title: Costume, Hair & Make-up

front: Why does Mrs Johnstone's costume improve slightly while Mrs Lyons' costume becomes dramatically worse?
answer: To show that honesty and love sustain Mrs Johnstone, while guilt and deception destroy Mrs Lyons from within.
title: Costume, Hair & Make-up

front: The set design for Blood Brothers must communicate three main location areas. Name them.
answer: Liverpool city centre (Johnstones) / Urban Liverpool (Lyons) / Skelmersdale
title: Set Design & Staging Types

front: Why is room for an orchestra essential when staging Blood Brothers?
answer: Because Blood Brothers is a musical, so the production needs space for live music.
title: Set Design & Staging Types

front: Why is black box staging unsuitable for Blood Brothers?
answer: There is no room for large set pieces, dance numbers or an orchestra, and no wings for exits.
title: Set Design & Staging Types

front: Blood Brothers uses six colours with symbolic meaning in lighting design. Name them.
answer: Red / Blue / Straw (warm yellow) / Green / White / Black (darkness)
title: Lighting & Sound Design

front: Why would a lighting designer use a cold blue wash in the prison scene?
answer: To create an atmosphere of isolation, working alongside sound design such as dripping water.
title: Lighting & Sound Design

front: Why do lighting and sound design shift from warm to cold between Act One and Act Two?
answer: To mirror the twins' loss of innocence and the growing sense that tragedy is inevitable.
title: Lighting & Sound Design

front: Stage directions serve three purposes in Blood Brothers. What are they?
answer: Practical information / Motivation / Emotion
title: Performance Skills & Semiotics

front: Russell uses six types of semiotic symbolism in Blood Brothers. Name them.
answer: Colour symbolism / Set symbolism / Sound symbolism / Proxemics / Lighting symbolism / Costume symbolism
title: Performance Skills & Semiotics

front: Why does the Narrator use deliberate pauses before key words in Blood Brothers?
answer: To build tension, adding to his measured, authoritative and controlled way of speaking.
title: Performance Skills & Semiotics

front: Why does Mickey increase his distance from Linda and Edward in Act Two?
answer: To show his emotional withdrawal from the people closest to him.
title: Performance Skills & Semiotics

front: A director staging the final scene of Blood Brothers considers four design areas. What are they?
answer: Blocking / Levels / Lighting / Sound
title: Key Scenes & Directing

front: The final scene's sound design unfolds in three parts. What are they, in order?
answer: The gunshot / Silence / Mrs Johnstone's song
title: Key Scenes & Directing

front: Why does Edward quietly exit while Mickey and Linda grow closer?
answer: It is the first suggestion to the audience that Edward loves Linda but respects Mickey too much to intervene.
title: Key Scenes & Directing

front: Why does the orchestra stop playing during the gunshot in the final scene?
answer: So the gunshot's sound can land with its full dramatic impact, undistracted by music.
title: Key Scenes & Directing

front: When writing about Rise Up's performance, the SEAS structure has four steps. Name them.
answer: State what you observed / Explain why it worked / Discuss audience impact / Suggest a development
title: Overview, Context & Style

front: Rise Up explores four key themes. What are they?
answer: Equality and racism / Relationships / Violence / Ambitions
title: Overview, Context & Style

front: Why did the American government not protect the Freedom Riders at first?
answer: It asked them to stop instead of protecting them from the violent attacks they faced.
title: Overview, Context & Style

front: Why did the Freedom Riders travel from Washington to the Southern States of America?
answer: To expose that segregation was still happening in the South despite laws banning it.
title: Overview, Context & Style

front: The bus explosion's sound collage layers four voices. What are they doing?
answer: Em repeating the Lord's Prayer / Uncle George shouting a threat / The Little White Girl narrating / Dayz panicking about being burned
title: Key Moments — White Shoppers & Bus Explosion

front: Why does the White Shoppers scene make the Little White Girl the focal point?
answer: To highlight her innocence and the importance of her questioning the shoppers' racism.
title: Key Moments — White Shoppers & Bus Explosion

front: Why does the bus scene contrast Em's calm stillness with Dayz's panic?
answer: To highlight how different people react differently when facing the same danger.
title: Key Moments — White Shoppers & Bus Explosion

front: Which four positions make up the diamond formation that opens the CJ Reminder scene, from highest to lowest?
answer: Ty as Jim (highest) / Em as Thora / Dayz as Merna / CJ as Hank (lowest)
title: Key Moments — Diane Nash & CJ Reminder

front: Six props on the steel flats create a visual reminder of the story so far. Name them.
answer: Confederate flag / Ku Klux Klan hat / Uncle George's cowboy hat / Bull Connor's hat / Kennedy's red tie / The Little White Girl's headband
title: Key Moments — Diane Nash & CJ Reminder

front: Why do the three Black actors circle and pin CJ against the flat in the Reminder scene?
answer: To make him feel the same intimidation and fear the Freedom Riders actually experienced.
title: Key Moments — Diane Nash & CJ Reminder

front: Why do all the actors relax their posture at the end of the CJ Reminder scene?
answer: To show the intimidation exercise is over and their rehearsal will simply continue.
title: Key Moments — Diane Nash & CJ Reminder

front: Rise Up uses five distinct lighting states for key moments. Name the moments they light.
answer: Bus explosion / Bull Connor scene / Final scenes / White Shoppers scene / Prison scene
title: Design & Performance Evaluation

front: Rise Up's sound design includes five key examples. Name them.
items: Hit the Road Jack by Ray Charles
answer: Hit the Road Jack by Ray Charles / Bus explosion sound effects / American national anthem snippets / Sound collage of layered voices / Children's voices about racism today
title: Design & Performance Evaluation

front: Why does CJ's casual costume contrast with Ty's formal one at the start of Rise Up?
answer: It implies CJ did not think the Freedom Riders were worth dressing up for.
title: Design & Performance Evaluation

front: Why does Rise Up use minimalistic costumes with no costume changes?
answer: So actors can switch characters quickly, keeping the performance flowing at a fast pace.
title: Design & Performance Evaluation
